slides.headline: He became Congress president at 35 - then spent over a decade building the system that still educates India today.
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was born November 11, 1888.
slides.body: A scholar, journalist, and freedom fighter, he became the youngest-ever president of the Indian National Congress in 1923, at age 35, and later held the longest presidential term in Congress history, from 1940 to 1946 - through years when most of the party's leadership, including Azad, was jailed by the British.

slides.headline: He became independent India's first Education Minister - and held the post for over a decade.
slides.body: From 1947 to 1958, Azad laid the foundations of India's modern education system, including the creation of the University Grants Commission. In 2008, the Indian government declared his birthday, November 11, as National Education Day.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat is built on the education systems its founders chose to prioritize from day one.
slides.body: Azad treated education as nation-building, not an afterthought - a decision whose institutions are still shaping India's workforce nearly eight decades later.
